basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 27.' and it opens '(Cap. XXIX.—Vers. 27.) Comple ergo hebdomadam istius: et dabo etiam hanc tibi. Postquam'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXIX.—Vers. 27.) Comple ergo hebdomadam istius: et dabo etiam hanc tibi. Postquam Liam Jacob fraude deceptus pro Rachel uxorem acceperat, dicitur ei a socero Laban ut septem dies post nuptias sororis prioris expleat, et sic accipiat Rachel, pro qua iterum septem annis aliis serviturus sit. Non igitur, ut quidam male aestimant, post septem annos alios Rachel accepit uxorem, sed post septem dies nuptiarum uxoris primae. Nam sequitur: Et ingressus est ad Rachel, et dilexit Rachel magis quam Liam, et servivit ei septem annis aliis (Gen. XXIX, 30).
